1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
This I.A. application has been filed for release of the appellant- petitioner on bail.

3. Heard learned counsels for the parties.
4.

It is stated by learned counsel for the appellant-petitioner that although initially allegation was made for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n)/313/417 of I.P.C. read with Section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (PoA) Act, after framing of the charge, the accused-Petitioner faced trial.

The learned trial court, after conclusion of the trial, found the accused-Petitioner guilty of offence under Sections 313/417 of the I.P.C. and he has been convicted thereunder and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of 7 years.
Further, it appears that the Petitioner has been acquitted of the charges under Sections 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (PoA) Act.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant-Petitioner in course of his argument, drew the attention of this court to the impugned judgment wherein the learned trial court has discussed the evidence vividly.

It appears that on analysis of the evidence, the learned trial court has arrived at the conclusion that Samir Kumar Parida vs State Of Odisha on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148292267/
1 the sexual relationship between the appellant and the victim was consensual.

sentences.text: Therefore, the appellant was not found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C.

However, the appellant has been found guilty of the offence punishable under Sections 313/417 of the I.P.C. as the victim was taken to a clinic for her abortion and it is alleged that the appellant was instrumental in taking her to such clinic.
6. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it appears that there is nothing with regard to the victim raising any objection to the abortion as it was done in a clinic under medical supervision.

Therefore,
that part of the evidence it appears to be a bit shaky.
In any event, the same shall be dealt with while hearing the appeal of the appellant.

7. Taking into consideration the fact that the appellant has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of 7 years and in the meantime he has already been undergone imprisonment for a period of 1 year and 5 months, this Court is inclined to release the Appellant- Petitioner on bail in Special Case No.55/2022 arising out of CIS No.151/2022, the court of learned Presiding Officer, Special Court (SC & ST), Balasore.
It is open for the Trial Court to impose any other conditions as may be deemed just and proper.
Violation of any of the conditions imposed by the trial court shall entail cancellation of the bail application.
8. Accordingly, the I.A. is disposed of.

9. Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
10.
List this matter in the week commencing 03.02.2025 for admission.

( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge Anil Location: High Court of Orissa Samir Kumar Parida vs State Of Odisha on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148292267/
